key_insight: A large, real-world interaction dataset (200k+ queries) shows how researchers use LLM-powered literature discovery and question-answering tools in short, iterative sessions—revealing distinct usage patterns, intent distributions, and reliance on retrieval-augmented responses.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of large-scale, real-world data on how scientists actually interact with AI research tools, enabling evidence-based design and evaluation of LLM-powered research interfaces.
method: Collected and anonymized >200,000 user queries and interaction logs from two deployed tools (literature discovery and scientific Q&A) within an LLM-powered retrieval-augmented generation platform.
Sessionized and categorized interactions by intent (e.g., discovery vs. direct Q&A), engagement metrics (session length, query reformulation), and system behavior (retrieval vs. generated output).
Analyzed usage patterns and engagement signals to surface common workflows, failure modes, and opportunities for UI and model improvements.
impact: Provides practitioners with empirical evidence to guide UI design, retrieval and prompt tuning, and evaluation metrics for scientific AI tools; supports creation of benchmarks and best practices rooted in real user behavior.
visual_elements: Dataset overview card: stacked counters (total queries, sessions, users) and timeline of data collection
User journey Sankey diagram: flows between discovery interface, Q&A interface, and next actions (refine, read paper, export)
Engagement heatmap/bar chart: query intents, session lengths, and reformulation rates by tool
System architecture diagram: RAG pipeline showing retrieval, LLM generation, and UI interaction points where logs were captured
paper_title: Understanding Usage and Engagement in AI-Powered Scientific Research Tools: The Asta Interaction Dataset
paper_authors: Dany Haddad, Dan Bareket, Joseph Chee Chang, Jay DeYoung, Jena D. Hwang
